attributes.law_screen: claim.law.direct-global-member-flips-index-base-association.20260831.v1 APPLIED and CONFIRMED in its cell (4). Its matrix says exactly one cell yields target's `add rBase,rIdx` + displacement: global SYMBOL reached through a member/array reference. The TU's PT(i) macro is cell (3) (global symbol + raw offset), which the law says is byte-for-byte identical to the pointer-local case and does NOT flip - matching our emitted `addi r28,r3,3136 / add / lwz 4(r28)` against target's `add r28,r31,r0 / lwz 3140(r28)`. Writing the same address as an array element + member moved it to cell (4) and reproduced the target. claim.law.local-alias-vs-direct-global-spelling-diverges.20260831.v1 and claim.law.IG_local-alias-of-a-global-root-pays-the-direct-global-tax.20260901.v1 screened: the local `p` is retained, and no extra symbol materialization appeared here because every use sits in ONE region (see the boundary law recorded separately).
attributes.probed_form: Added next to the existing PT macro: `#define PTA(i)        (&((Player*)((u8*)potionicon_tab + 0xC40))[i])`. Then in write_health_and_items only: `rgb = ((u32*)(tab + 1408))[PTA(i)->class_id];` and `p = PTA(i);`, replacing the two `PT(i)` spellings. No other PT() site was changed.
attributes.residual: Two clusters remain, both classified. (1) @0x24c a two-instruction slwi reorder (schedule-class). (2) @0x608 an EQUIVALENT-COPY-FORM: target emits `li r25,0` then `addi r24,r25,0` - initialising the byte-offset induction as a COPY of the loop counter's zero - where we emit two independent `li ...,0`. Confirmed compiler-internal by reading the loop body (@0x610-0x628): the source `for (j = 0; j < 7; j++) mbBlitInit3414(pm_blit[i][j], 1);` has exactly ONE variable, so the second zero has no source spelling. Both sides then run identical `addi rJ,rJ,1 / cmpwi rJ,7 / addi rOff,rOff,4 / blt`. This is a candidate for the WebFrank equivalent-copy-form class (claim.LZ_webfrank-equivalent-copy-form-edit-class.20260901.v1), not a source axis.
